page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.t5-c1m2.4xlarge is a burstable instance type built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 architecture. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz, configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage is bundled with this instance, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight the performance characteristics of the burstable CPU allocation. Single-core performance is constrained, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the weak and poor categories respectively. However, multi-core benchmarks, such as stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, achieve average tier results. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also perform in the average range, though the PassMark memory score is weak. Cryptographic and vector instruction sets, including AVX-512 and AES, are supported, which aids multi-threaded decompression and database operations.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.t5-c1m2.4xlarge is its burstable CPU credit model. While it offers a high vCPU count relative to its qualitative cost profile, sustained high CPU utilization will deplete credits, leading to throttled performance. This makes the instance cost-efficient for workloads with variable or spikey demand rather than continuous heavy computation. It is suited for static web serving, development environments, code compilation, and lightweight database operations that do not require sustained peak CPU performance.
